title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 3: catholic doctrine — opposite always Pelagian/Semipelagian badge; they grant common offered mercy but make healing grace hang on prior merit
pass_a_gloss: That this was the doctrine of the Catholic Church is plain, 1. Because the contrary was always defended by the Pelagians and Semipelagians, and held as it were their proper badge. For although (as the Arminians also now do) they acknowledged a certain grace offered unto all from God’s mere mercy, yet that which heals, quickens, and justifies, and which is not only offered on God’s part, but is already possessed on man’s part—that, I say, they thought given only from antecedent merit of some good operation or disposition which God saw in the receiver, and did not see in others.
pass_b_english: That this was catholic church doctrine is plain, first because the contrary was always the Pelagians’ and Semipelagians’ defense and as it were their badge. Though (as Arminians also now do) they granted a grace offered to all from mere mercy, yet the grace that heals, quickens, and justifies—and is not only offered by God but already possessed by man—they thought given only from antecedent merit of some good act or disposition God saw in the receiver and not in others.
source_text: Hanc fuisse doctrinam Catholicae Ecclesiae patet, 1. Quia contraria semper a Pelagianis et Semipelagianis defensa fuit, et ejus ea quasi proprium insigne habita. Nam utcunque (quod etiam Arminiani jam faciunt) gratiam quandam agnoverint ex mera Dei misericordia omnibus oblatam, tamen illam quae sanat, vivificat, et justificat, quaeque non offertur tantum ex parte Dei, sed jam possidetur ex parte hominis, illam, inquam, cenrebant datam nisi ex antecedente merito bonae alicujus operationis aut dispositionis quam in accipiente vidit Deus, in aliis non vidit.
